correctness.rationale: Let U be union of a incomparable lower Boolean sets; Sperner bounds a≤binom(|U|,floor(|U|/2)), hence |U|≥mu(a). With b>=2 incomparable upper sets, no upper is U, so rank ≥mu(a)+1. Minimal mu(a) forces any a selected central-layer subsets of [mu(a)] to cover all mu(a) coordinates, since otherwise Sperner on mu(a)-1 coordinates would contradict minimality. Adding b distinct new coordinates to that union gives b incomparable upper sets of size mu(a)+1. At minimum rank the lower union has size exactly mu(a) and each upper must be union plus a distinct new coordinate; w*=mu(a)+b follows, as does w*=a+b iff a=2,3,4. Checked mu(a) for a=2..15; the Sperner/union argument proves all a,b≥2.
residual_risks: The theorem excludes a=1 or b=1 and refers to width optimized at minimum rank, not arbitrary-width induced embeddings.
